title: Fourier bound for functions far from linear
statement:
Fix an integer $k \ge 2$ and let $f : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$ be $\varepsilon$-far from linear in the normalized sense: that is, $f(0) = 0$, the parameter satisfies $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and $\dist(f, g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear $g : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$. Write $\widetilde{f}(x) = \omega_k^{f(x)}$ for the lift of $f$ to the unit circle, where $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$, and let $\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)$ denote its Fourier coefficient at frequency $s$. Then for every $s \in \bbz_k^n$,
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\bigl[\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\,\varepsilon.
\]
hypotheses_covered: dist(f,g) ≥ ε for every linear g
s is an arbitrary frequency in ℤ_k^n
